This cichlid was only scientifically described as Nannacara adoketa in 1993 and was for a long time one of the absolute dream fish of cichlid enthusiasts. The initially very few imported fish were mostly exported to Japan and insane prices were demanded – and paid!

Nowadays, the initial situation has eased considerably. Ivanacara adoketa is regularly offered both as offspring and occasionally as a wild catch. This species, which is demanding in terms of water quality during breeding and rearing, will probably never be a “cheap fish”, but the prices have fallen to such an extent that anyone seriously interested can probably afford them.
The species occurs only in a narrowly defined area on the middle Rio Negro. Its distribution area is far removed from that of the other Nannacara species.

The fish require soft and acidic water for their well-being; these values are essential for breeding. The temperature should be between 23 and 26°C; the animals prefer it a little cooler than too warm. Breeding is also successful at temperatures around 24°C.
The males grow to around 8-9 cm long, the females remain around 3 cm smaller.
They are open brooders with a parent family. Soft, acidic water is essential for breeding, and the species is demanding in terms of water quality during breeding and rearing.

The species differs in many respects from the other Nannacara species, which led to the genus Ivanacara being established for it, together with the also very different N. bimaculata. N. bimaculata is very similar to N. adoketa but is endemic, occurring exclusively in the Potaro and Essequibo rivers in Guyana.
